variants.headline: Our new vassalage under {{master}}
body: The treaty that makes us a vassal of {{master}} is signed, and our flag now flies beside theirs. In the chancery, a clerk copied the terms twice and sealed both copies before the wax cooled. From today, their court speaks for us in matters we once settled alone.

variants.headline: An era of our own counsel, concluded
body: The years in which our {{terms.civic.government}} answered to no other court are ended. This season we became a vassal of {{master}}, and the treaty lies in the archive under a fresh seal. A scribe has closed the old roll with a black ribbon, and the new one begins with their name at the top.

variants.headline: Tell us what protection we bought
body: Word came at dawn that we are now vassals of {{master}}, and the {{terms.civic.government}} has still not read the terms aloud. Ask the first clerk you meet what we promised and what we received. If our young men can be called to their wars, the square deserves to hear the bargain before the drums do.

variants.headline: Our neighbors have a new court to bargain with
body: A dispute with us now runs through two courts instead of one. Our vassalage to {{master}} means their ministers can be asked to settle what our own envoys once decided. The open question is whether the {{player.civic.government}} of {{master}} treats that duty as a shield or as a leash.

variants.headline: Our defensive pact with {{ally}} is over
body: The defensive pact with {{ally}} has lapsed, and the foreign office has filed the papers without ceremony. The two countries remain at peace, so no column marches and no harbor closes. What has ended is the promise that an attack on one would bring the other.

variants.headline: An attack on {{ally}} is their problem now
body: Staff officers who once wrote {{ally}}'s name into a war plan must now erase it. The pact is gone, and with it the certainty of a second army on the flank. A general can still win alone; he simply has less room to be wrong.

variants.headline: Will you still send the next load?
body: Sir, I heard at the exchange that the pact with {{ally}} is finished, and a factor across that border asked me whether our trade would follow it down. I told him no. His people have weighed my goods honestly for years, and I will not stop trusting a whole nation because two courts have stopped promising to fight for each other.

variants.headline: We sign a defensive pact with {{ally}}
body: The defensive pact with {{ally}} is signed, and the crier had the news before the ink was dry. Under its terms, an attack on either country brings both to the field. The promise is simple to state and heavy to keep.

variants.headline: Hear it! We stand with {{ally}}
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The pact with {{ally}} is sealed, and the seal is still warm. Strike at them and you strike at us; that is the whole of it. Carry that word to every gate and every well!

variants.headline: A pact for the {{terms.civic.government}}, a question for the street
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} has promised that our soldiers will answer for {{ally}}. The clerks who signed it will not be the ones who march. Before the first recruit is called, read the terms where he drills, so he knows whose quarrel he is buying with his own blood.

variants.headline: Letters from the {{terms.civic.government}}: a pact with {{ally}}
body: We are credibly informed that a defensive pact has been concluded between our {{terms.civic.government}} and {{ally}}. In a quiet season such a paper asks almost nothing of either people. Let a third power grow bold, and it asks for everything.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} denounces our nation
body: {{civilization}} has denounced us in public, and the declaration was read on the steps of the foreign ministry this morning. No treaty was torn up to mark the occasion, and no envoy was called home. What has been spent is the courtesy that made quiet dealings possible.

variants.headline: The square heard it first
body: The fishmonger heard it before the fish were sold: {{civilization}} has denounced us. From there the news ran stall to stall, gathering a regiment, a stolen cannon and a duchess along the way. By dusk the market had a better story than the ministry and was not inclined to give it up.

variants.headline: Let the denunciation be answered
body: {{civilization}} has called us out by name, and every court in the world has heard it. Fine words will not unsay the insult; a stronger guard on the frontier might. Let the ministers answer with a muster, not a memorandum.

variants.headline: In this year, {{civilization}} spoke against us
body: In this year {{player.leader}}, {{player.civic.leaderTitle}} of {{civilization}}, spoke a denunciation of our nation before assembled witnesses. The scribe has set down the words in full and marked the day beside them. No answer is entered in this record yet.

variants.headline: First contact with {{stranger}}
body: Our envoys have met the people of {{stranger}} for the first time, and both sides now know each other by name. The meeting was formal, and the account of it fills several pages. Whatever comes next, it will begin with a conversation rather than a guess.

variants.headline: They say strangers came over the hill
body: They say two hunters followed a line of cut branches to the river and found a camp of {{stranger}} drying fish. Nobody could speak a word the others knew, so they traded a knife for a handful of salt and sat down together. The tale has been told at every hearth since, and the knife is still on the shelf.

variants.headline: A new people, and new roads to walk
body: Letters from the frontier relate that our envoys and the envoys of {{stranger}} have met and exchanged greetings. The first words were cautious, as first words are, but a written account now exists, copied for each court. Both courts may address each other by name, and honest maps may follow.

variants.headline: We just met {{stranger}}
body: First contact with {{stranger}}, confirmed this week. Names exchanged, gifts logged, no trouble. More when the envoys file their report.

variants.headline: The mapmaker has a question about {{stranger}}
body: Sir, since the news of {{stranger}} reached my shop, three customers have asked for a chart of country I have never crossed. I will not draw a coast on hearsay. Lend me the survey notes from the meeting, and my next map will be thin on ornament and sound on every line.

variants.headline: {{first}} and {{second}} sign a defensive pact
body: By noon the exchange clerks were repeating it: {{first}} and {{second}} have signed a defensive pact. A broker read the notice twice, then raised his rate for anyone carrying goods between the two. A quarrel with one of them now has a second name attached.

variants.headline: The pact between {{first}} and {{second}} redraws the arithmetic
body: The pact between {{first}} and {{second}} has changed what a war on that frontier would cost. A campaign against either court must now expect a second army from an unexpected direction. That may keep the peace through fear, or gather several small quarrels into one large one. The answer will be written at a border, not at a signing table.

variants.headline: From abroad: {{first}} and {{second}} stand together
body: Letters from abroad relate that {{first}} and {{second}} have agreed to stand together in war. In our own market, a draper who buys cloth from both countries has split his next order between them. Should one frontier close, he means to have goods coming through the other.

variants.headline: {{first}} and {{second}} end their defensive pact
body: The defensive pact between {{first}} and {{second}} has been dissolved, and the news arrived without a ceremony to mark it. No soldiers have moved against either country. The pledge that each would answer for the other is now only a line in an old file.

variants.headline: The quiet between {{first}} and {{second}}
body: For a while, an envoy weighing a quarrel with {{first}} also had to weigh {{second}}. That second calculation has just been struck out. Each court must now be read on its own temper, with no paper tying one answer to the other. The change will show first in smaller demands and slower promises.

variants.headline: The fence between two gardens
body: Two farms shared one watchdog until each built a gate of its own. The dog now sleeps at whichever gate smells of supper.

variants.headline: We declare friendship with {{friend}}
body: The friendship between our nation and {{friend}} is now declared in public. At the granary, a clerk pinned the notice beside the salt price, where everyone would see it. Merchants on both sides can plan their seasons as if the goodwill will hold.

variants.headline: Hear it! Friendship with {{friend}}
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! {{friend}} stands as a friend of this nation, and the declaration is signed. A friend at the gate, a friend at the market, a friend when the road is long! Pass the word to the back of the crowd!

variants.headline: Sir, a good word travels slowly
body: Sir, I haul freight between your country and {{friend}}, and I learned of the new friendship at the last inn before the border. The drivers there were quicker to pass the cup and slower to argue about the road. I hope the courts keep it that way, since my children eat from what that road pays.

variants.headline: The tavern drank to {{friend}} last night
body: The crier had barely finished when the tavern keeper put a jug on the counter and poured the first cup to {{friend}}. Nobody had asked him to, and he did not wait for applause. A friendly road means carts, he said, and carts mean drivers with a thirst.

variants.headline: Our friendship with {{friend}} is over
body: The friendship with {{friend}} has been withdrawn, and the notice went up without a speech. At the wool exchange, a broker has stopped pairing their houses with ours in the same quotation. The warmth that once made a bargain easy has gone out of the relationship.

variants.headline: In memoriam: the friendship with {{friend}}
body: The friendship between our people and {{friend}} was once raised in toasts at every public dinner, the glasses lifted without a doubting word behind them. That declaration has now been withdrawn, and the toasts have fallen quiet. What remains between us and {{friend}} is an old habit of courtesy, which may yet outlast the paper that ended it.

variants.headline: The end of the {{friend}} friendship, weighed
body: The friendship with {{friend}} is over, and the record is thinner for it. No troops were promised under that declaration, but confidence was, and confidence is what a merchant adds to the price of a road. Watch the correspondence from that capital grow shorter before anyone raises a voice.

variants.headline: Our court takes {{vassal}} as a vassal
body: {{vassal}} now answers to our {{terms.civic.government}} as a vassal. A clerk at the palace has entered their name on the roll of dependent courts, in fresh ink. The tribute will be counted when it arrives; the duty to protect them begins at once.

variants.headline: {{vassal}} entered in the roll of vassals
body: In this season the envoys of {{vassal}} came before our court and placed their nation under our protection. Their {{player.civic.government}} keeps its hall, its officers and its seal. A new column has been ruled in the tribute book, and the first entry awaits the year's end.

variants.headline: A new source of tribute, a new frontier to defend
body: Tribute from {{vassal}} will soon reach our treasury, and the sum will be welcome. The obligation that comes with it is harder to price: a vassal expects help, and help must travel by road. The value of this arrangement depends on how quickly our soldiers can reach their frontier.

variants.headline: Let the magistrates of {{vassal}} set out what they can pay
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} may now set a tribute on {{vassal}}, and the square is already spending it. A figure that pleases the crowd will empty the treasury twice: once when the tax cannot be paid, and again when the province must be held by force. Let the assessors count the harvest first, then take a share the land can carry.

variants.headline: {{vassal}} is no longer our vassal
body: {{vassal}} no longer owes tribute or obedience to our court. The tribute office struck their name from the roll this morning and closed the old account. The two governments now meet as equals, which may prove easier or harder than the old arrangement.

variants.headline: {{vassal}} walks free of us
body: {{vassal}} has slipped out of our protection, and the frontier garrison feels it before the capital does. A captain who counted their militia in his dispositions must now find those men elsewhere or do without. Every court that still pays us tribute is watching how we answer.

variants.headline: The vassalage of {{vassal}} comes to an end
body: The vassalage of {{vassal}} has ended, and neither court has asked for a farewell ceremony. Clerks who once copied their accounts into our ledgers have been given other desks. A sealed treaty sits in a drawer, and the couriers who once rode north now ride elsewhere.

variants.headline: We and {{civilization}} denounce each other
body: {{civilization}} and our {{terms.civic.government}} have denounced each other, both in the same season. The two declarations are public, and neither court has left itself an easy way back. At the exchange, a broker read both notices and added a surcharge to every crate bound that way.

variants.headline: Both courts put their quarrel on record
body: Each court has now put its quarrel with the other in writing, ours and {{civilization}}'s alike. Envoys may still meet behind closed doors, but both sides have said in public what is hard to unsay. Every small dispute from here will be measured against that record.

variants.headline: Two houses, one quarrel
body: Two farmers curse each other over the hedge. The hedge grows thicker, and neither field grows wider.

variants.headline: Who pays for the shouting?
body: Words have passed between our {{terms.civic.government}} and {{civilization}}, and the cost will land in some ordinary street. A printer near the market has already set the same quarrel twice, once for each side, and been paid for both. Let the government name the trade it is willing to lose before it names another grievance.

variants.headline: We open our borders to {{civilization}}
body: The frontier is open to travelers from {{civilization}} as of this morning, and the first carts rolled through before the midday bell. No permit is required at the posts, and the gate clerks have been told to keep their ledgers ready. Our land is theirs to cross, and our garrisons will see many new faces.

variants.headline: Notice to merchants: our roads are open to {{civilization}}
body: Notice to merchants: from this morning, the frontier stands open to {{civilization}}. Their caravans may cross without a new permit and trade wherever they find a buyer. Gate clerks have been warned to expect a long line and to keep it moving.

variants.headline: Open borders with {{civilization}}, and the goodwill they carry
body: The border now stands open to {{civilization}}, which puts their wagons on our roads and their coin in our markets. It also gives their court a stake in keeping the frontier calm, since a closed road costs them as much as us. A crossing that carries goods both ways is cheaper to keep than a line of soldiers.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} opens its borders to us
body: The posts of {{civilization}} have been told to let our people pass, and a courier tried the order yesterday without showing a paper. Their roads are open to our caravans and our letters alike. The welcome is new, and it is worth using before the mood changes.

variants.headline: The road to {{capital}} is open
body: With {{civilization}} lifting its permit, the road to {{capital}} is open to our caravans. A carter who has quoted that route cautiously for years now promises a faster run and a cheaper rate. His regular customers are already asking when the next wagon leaves.

variants.headline: One wagon, loaded by noon
body: The carter at the north gate loaded his wagon by noon, and not with goods for market. Word had reached him that {{civilization}} had opened its border, so he packed a blanket and a loaf and pointed the horse at the gap. "A man should see a country before he sells to it," he said.

variants.headline: {{from}} and {{to}} bargain, and a war ends
body: {{from}} and {{to}} have reached an agreement, and folded into it is peace with a third state. In the border town, a shopkeeper has begun taking the boards from her windows, though she has been disappointed before. This time the promise came with two signatures and a date.

variants.headline: The terms, as recorded
body: {{from}} brings: {{fromGives}}.
{{to}} brings: {{toGives}}.
Chief among the entries: a third country's war ends at this table, without its seal.

variants.headline: A war ends at someone else's table
body: Peace reaches a third state through a bargain between {{from}} and {{to}}, and that state never sat at the table. Its officers will learn the terms from a rider who arrives long after the ink has dried. Wars ended this way stop quickly and leave the men who fought them wondering what was traded above their heads.

variants.headline: War is written into the deal between {{from}} and {{to}}
body: {{from}} and {{to}} have concluded a bargain, and written into it is a war against a third state. At the posting house, a courier called for a fresh horse and would not say where he was riding. The stable boy saw the direction and kept it to himself.

variants.headline: Tonight: a deal that buys a war
body: Tonight, {{from}} and {{to}} signed a deal, and a war is part of what they bought. The third country in the terms has said nothing yet. Our reporters are on that border, and we will tell you what happens next.

variants.headline: Other people's wars, other people's coin
body: The bargain between {{from}} and {{to}} pays for itself with a third nation's peace, and that nation was not asked. Our government had no seat at the table, and no plan has been published for the roads and cargo that will now cross a war zone. It should tell the country who will guard that trade, and with how many men.

variants.headline: Our vassalage to {{master}} is over
body: The vassalage to {{master}} is over, and the tribute rolls have been closed. Our {{terms.civic.government}} now issues its own orders without waiting for another court's seal. The first real test will come when a neighbor asks who speaks for us and expects a foreign name.

variants.headline: Hear it! We bow no more
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The claim of {{master}} is dead, and our {{terms.civic.government}} answers to no one above it. No tribute, no borrowed orders, no bowed head! Tell the square, tell the gate, tell anyone who asks who rules here!

variants.headline: In this year, the vassalage was dissolved
body: In this year our nation ceased to be a vassal of {{master}}, and the payments to that court stopped. The scribe has noted the return of our seal and the departure of their resident envoy. What use the court makes of that seal is left for a later hand to write.

variants.headline: Free, and with work to do
body: {{terms.civic.people}}, the oath to {{master}} is broken, and not a moment too soon. Our {{terms.civic.government}} must now prove it can stand without a patron leaning on its shoulder. Let every envoy's instructions be read in public before he rides out, so the nation hears what is said in its name.

variants.headline: We denounce {{civilization}}
body: Our {{terms.civic.government}} has denounced {{civilization}}, and the words are now part of the public record. Clerks have copied the declaration into the day book, where any foreign court may read it. The anger may pass; the page will not.

variants.headline: Said plainly, and none too soon
body: {{civilization}} has been denounced at last, and the declaration stands signed in our own hand. That is a firm word where too many careful ones were spent before it, and every court on the frontier has taken note. Now bring the garrisons up to the same pitch, so {{civilization}} weighs our spears as carefully as it has just read our resolve.

variants.byline: A reader who trades across that border
variants.headline: Sir, was there no quieter road?
body: Sir, I read this morning that our {{terms.civic.government}} has denounced {{civilization}}, and my first thought was of the wagons that cross that border in both directions. A quarrel is cheap to announce and expensive to feed. If there is a way to take back the edge without taking back the truth, the government should find it.

variants.headline: In this year, we spoke against {{civilization}}
body: In this year the {{terms.civic.government}} spoke against {{civilization}} in the hearing of foreign courts. The scribe has copied the declaration word for word and dated it. No judgment is entered beside it, for the consequences are not yet known.
